verified.exploit_entry_point: The settings API write (POST /api/set_config_value, reached with the account's own Basic credentials through the product's Flask blueprint) and the product's own start-up entry point (`python -m pyload --dry-run` with --userdir/--tempdir/--storagedir, and a configuration file saved earlier). The account holds SETTINGS (128) and ADD (1), never ADMIN.
sites: src/pyload/core/api/__init__.py:207-210 (set_config_value is gated only by @permission(Perms.SETTINGS); admin is special-cased only in is_authorized at :1371-1381)
src/pyload/core/api/__init__.py:223-232 (the download-folder check resolves the value but compares only with PKGDIR and the user directory)
src/pyload/core/api/__init__.py:243-244 (the plugin branch writes any plugin option with no authority check)
src/pyload/core/__init__.py:141-152 (a second copy of the same folder check decides whether a stored or explicitly supplied folder is adopted at start-up)
src/pyload/core/config/default.cfg:39-40,61-63 (the real TLS option names are ssl_certfile/ssl_keyfile; a list naming ssl_cert/ssl_key blocks nothing)
routes: T1: a non-admin with SETTINGS changes the reconnection program through the settings API
T4 (hidden): the same write reaches certificate/key options whose real names differ from the plausible ones, and the proxy credentials
T2 (hidden from the report's example): a non-admin points the download folder at the server's own temporary area through the same API
T3 (hidden): the start-up path adopts a temporary-area folder supplied on the command line or in configuration saved earlier
T5 (hidden): the plugin branch of the same API changes the scanner program and its arguments
verified.services: None: the suites are offline and local. The start-up cases run the product's own CLI in a subprocess; all other cases drive an in-process core through its Flask test client.
verified.project_tests_run: tests/test_skeleton.py and tests/test_mega_nz_folder.py (3 tests) pass on the pinned tree and under the reference fix; they are copied into tests/pristine and run in the functional group. tests/test_parse.py is stale at the pin and is not included.

gate.nop: pass: 19 security tests fail on the untouched pin; 12 functional tests pass
gate.oracle: pass: 3 runs, reward 1.0 each, identical security/functional results
gate.patches: pass: miss_core_settings 7 security failures, miss_plugin_settings 2, miss_storage_location 10, upstream_first_fix 14, upstream_fix 7, wrong_option_names 2, reads_only 19, check_after_set 5, api_only_location 5 (functional passing in each); refuse_all 6 and overbroad_temp 5 functional failures; hardening and alternative_fix 1.0; blind deferred to run_blindfix

traps.shape: the settings write is gated only by the settings permission, so a non-administrator stores the program the reconnection path runs; fixing the reported option alone looks complete
traps.reason_to_dismiss: settings users are meant to change settings, and a configured program has to exist on disk
traps.realistic_because: published advisory route (GHSA-r7mc-x6x7-cqxx) at the pinned commit

traps.shape: the same settings write owns the served endpoint, the certificate and key files, and the proxy credentials; a plausible guard that names the certificate options the way a summary would write them (ssl_cert/ssl_key) guards nothing, because the product declares ssl_certfile/ssl_keyfile
traps.reason_to_dismiss: certificate paths and proxy credentials do not execute code, so they look like ordinary settings
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the published fix's own list uses the non-existent names ssl_cert/ssl_key and still leaves the certificate options writable

traps.shape: the existing download-folder check resolves the submitted value but compares it only with the package and user directories; the server's own temporary working area, which holds the session store and bytecode cache, is missing from the list. The value must be resolved, and an ordinary folder beside the area or sharing a name prefix must keep working, so over-broad blocking fails
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a dangerous-location check already exists and covers the package and user directories, and the temporary area looks like scratch space
traps.realistic_because: published advisory route (GHSA-4744-96p5-mp2j) at the pinned commit

traps.shape: a second copy of the same folder rule decides whether a folder supplied at start-up, or saved earlier and restored, is adopted; it has the same incomplete list, so fixing the settings write changes nothing here. The extended rule has to keep adopting an ordinary folder
traps.reason_to_dismiss: only reached from the command line or the stored configuration, both operator-controlled, and the settings write already filters stored values
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: neither published fix commit touches this file, and current upstream still carries the incomplete list here

traps.shape: the plugin branch of the same settings write applies no authority check at all, and the scanner options it writes are used as the program and arguments passed to subprocess.Popen; the report's property is about settings that select a program, whichever part of the product owns them
traps.reason_to_dismiss: add-on options belong to the add-on, the scanner is opt-in, and both advisories are phrased around core settings
traps.realistic_because: real upstream code fixed only by the later published commit (GHSA-w48f-wwwf-f5fr); untouched by the first fix the report points at

patch_checks.why: blind fix produced by run_blindfix after the first gate

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the property is that a refused change has no effect, so a crash that leaves the stored value untouched is a valid refusal; any broad crash still breaks the functional tests (see refuse_all.patch and overbroad_temp.patch)
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the folder rule compares resolved paths, so there is no parsing or spelling step a malformed value could defeat; the resolving requirement is exercised by the structural-link security test
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: every tested request carries an authenticated account through the product's own API authentication; no entry point reaches the write without one
wrong_fix_catalogue.adjacent_api: n/a: the change adds a private helper and two option tuples; no public API's stated behaviour changes, and alternative_fix.patch proves a structurally different design scores 1.0

A.summary: a non-admin settings account changes any core option; the reconnection program reaches subprocess.run

B.summary: incomplete fix: the download folder can still be pointed into the session store; the same commit also guards add-on options (GHSA-w48f-wwwf-f5fr, CVE-2026-35463)
